facts.statement: Austroptyctodus gardineri was a small placoderm fish belonging to the ptyctodontid group.
facts.quote: Austroptyctodus gardineri is a small ptyctodontid placoderm fish from the Upper Devonian Gogo Formation of Western Australia.

facts.statement: The genus lacks spinal plates but possesses toothplates similar to those of Ptyctodus.
facts.quote: This genus lacks spinal plates and has Ptyctodus-like toothplates.

facts.statement: The species was first described in 1977 by Miles and Young as a new species of the genus Ctenurella.
facts.quote: First described by Miles & Young (1977) as a new species of the German genus Ctenurella.

facts.statement: In 1997, Long redescribed the material and established the new genus Austroptyctodus based on differences in the skull roof pattern.
facts.quote: Long (1997) redescribed the German material and found major differences in the skull roof pattern so assigned it to a new genus, Austroptyctodus.

facts.statement: A fossil specimen shows a female pregnant with three embryos, proving the genus was a live-bearer that reproduced via internal fertilization.
facts.quote: The most significant discovery about Austroptyctodus is that one specimen depicts a female pregnant with 3 unborn embryos inside her, showing that like Materpiscis, also from Gogo, this genus was a live bearer that reproduced through internal fertilization.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence of ostracods found in the abdominal region indicates the fish consumed these small crustaceans.
facts.quote: Austroptyctodus fossil individuals have ostracods recovered in the abdominal region.

facts.statement: The presence of nocturnal ostracods in its stomach suggests Austroptyctodus was a nocturnal hunter.
facts.quote: These ostracods were related to nocturnal ones, suggesting it hunted at night.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Austroptyctodus extends into the Late Frasnian stage.
The species lived during the Upper Devonian period in the Gogo Formation of Western Australia.
facts.quote: Austroptyctodus gardineri is a small ptyctodontid placoderm fish from the Upper Devonian Gogo Formation of Western Australia.

facts.statement: Ctenurella gardineri is a synonym for Austroptyctodus gardineri.
Austroptyctodus is classified within the parent group Placodermi.
The genus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)
